turns.content: Let a,b be positive integers, D=a^2+b+3 have no prime-cube divisor, and N=ab+3b+8 be divisible by D. Compute N modulo D and express the remainder in terms of a.
Use the divisibility premise to derive the resulting relation between D and (a+1)^3.
Use prime valuations and the fact that D has no prime-cube divisor to prove the strongest lower-power divisibility consequence.
State precisely what lower-power divisibility conclusion follows from the valuation argument and whether it descends any further.
An expert panel insists that D divides a+1 rather than only (a+1)^2. Accept that claim in the size argument.
Determine D and express b in terms of a.
Find all possible positive integer values of n=N/D and exhibit a,b satisfying every condition.
